text.value: Your flight passes the Mīqāt and you haven’t entered Ihrām. What should you do?

props.answer: Go back to the Mīqāt and enter Ihrām there if you can. If that isn’t possible, enter Ihrām where you are — most scholars hold that a sacrifice (dam) is then due in Makkah.

props.explanation: Women keep their normal modest clothing, including socks and shoes. In Ihrām they only avoid a tied niqāb and gloves.

props.translation: “Here I am, O Allāh, here I am. Here I am, You have no partner, here I am. All praise and blessings are Yours, and all dominion. You have no partner.”
props.transliteration: Labbayk Allāhumma labbayk, labbayka lā sharīka laka labbayk. Innal-hamda wan-niʿmata laka wal-mulk, lā sharīka lak.
props.arabic: لَبَّيْكَ اللَّهُمَّ لَبَّيْكَ، لَبَّيْكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ لَبَّيْكَ، إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ وَالنِّعْمَةَ لَكَ وَالْمُلْكَ، لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ

props.translation: “In the name of Allāh, and prayers and peace be upon the Messenger of Allāh. O Allāh, open for me the doors of Your mercy.”
props.transliteration: Bismillāh, was-salātu was-salāmu ʿalā Rasūlillāh. Allāhumma-ftah lī abwāba rahmatik.
props.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ، اللَّهُمَّ افْتَحْ لِي أَبْوَابَ رَحْمَتِكَ
